olivia-cs: Heads up — Acme just filed a block: when their app triggers two tool calls at once (geocode + enrich) results are occasionally swapped and the downstream schema validation fails. They sent a minimal repro. :frowning:

olivia-cs: repro (curl) — they call the API with a single user request that our router fans out to both tools: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' 
 -d '{"input":"Locate and enrich: '1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy'","tools":["geocode","enrich"],"parallel":true}'
```

sam-eng: thanks. do we have the request_id/trace? any logs from the runtime? :eyes:

olivia-cs: req_id=acme-req-9932, trace=trace-0a1b2c3d, customer timestamp 2026-03-17T18:12:21Z. They included one failing response: second tool returned `null` for `lat/lon` and validation error: `expected object with lat,lon but got string`.

kevin-ops: digging into the runtime logs for trace-0a1b2c3d. I'm seeing two outgoing tool calls both stamped with the same `outbound_call_id` in a tiny time window — looks like a race where the call id assignment is happening on a shared stack var. Also saw repeated cache key `kv_prefix:addr-1600` for both. possible KV cache collision.

alex-repro: I ran the curl locally against staging and got a consistent repro when staging concurrency >=3. Here are the relevant log lines (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-17T18:12:21.101Z] trace-0a1b2c3d outbound_call_id=call-42 tool=geocode -> sent
[2026-03-17T18:12:21.102Z] trace-0a1b2c3d outbound_call_id=call-42 tool=enrich -> sent
[2026-03-17T18:12:21.210Z] trace-0a1b2c3d tool_result assoc_id=null tool=enrich result={...}
[2026-03-17T18:12:21.211Z] trace-0a1b2c3d tool_result assoc_id=call-42 tool=geocode result={lat:37.4,long:-122.0}
```
alex-repro: you can see both got the same outbound_call_id and one assoc_id is null. That lines up with the swapped/validation error.

infra-bot: Incident INC-4521 created and assigned to eng-runtime.canary.

maria-support: escalated to oncall, pinged customer with temporary mitigation: set `parallel=false` for now and we will follow up. Customer accepted the workaround. :ok_hand:

sam-eng: preliminary root cause hypothesis: when the request fanout spins up tool calls we reuse a non-thread-safe counter/slot to generate `outbound_call_id`. Under high concurrency the slot overwrites before the mapping to `tool_result` is fully materialized, causing either duplicated ids or null assoc ids. Also KV prefix generation using the same key without per-call UUID exacerbates collisions.

kevin-ops: agreed. quick patch: 1) switch to crypto UUID per outbound tool call, 2) ensure assoc_id is attached synchronously before async dispatch, 3) add a short-lived guard in KV keys (append call uuid). I'll push a canary to runtime-prod in 30m.

sam-eng: I'll draft a test to reproduce at scale and add a unit that asserts `outbound_call_id` uniqueness across fanout. Also adding a schema-gate: if tool_result assoc_id missing -> reject response and surface a 502 with actionable error to caller until runtime fix ships.

olivia-cs: Customer wants ETA. I'll tell them that a canary patch is going out in ~30m and we'll force a rollback if any regression. Also note they should keep `parallel=false` for critical workflows.

kevin-ops: rolling canary now to 5% canary nodes (runtime-canary-05). will report back with logs and metrics (assoc_id uniqueness rate).

maria-support: thanks team. I'll coordinate the customer update and keep the ticket open until we see stable metrics.

sam-eng: follow-up action items: add UUID per tool call (PR#4829), schema-gate on assoc_id (PR#4830), unit+load tests, and a dashboard for assoc_id uniqueness.

olivia-cs: noted, closing customer loop after canary is green. :white_check_mark:
